title: Financial ML Design and Governance Check

questions.question: What is the safest way to define a financial ML problem?
options: Name the decision, decision time, available evidence, action owner, error costs, and fallback
Choose the model family with the highest public benchmark score
Optimize one offline metric before defining the policy action
Collect every field currently present in the warehouse
questions.explanation: The prediction exists to support a bounded decision. Its timing, authority, consequences, and fallback determine the useful model contract.

questions.question: A chargeback is filed 18 days after a card authorization. How should it be used?
options: As a delayed label signal, never as a feature for that authorization decision
As a real-time feature because it exists in the warehouse now
As both label and feature to improve recall
It should be discarded from all training and monitoring
questions.explanation: The chargeback can help determine the later outcome, but it was not available when the authorization decision was made.

questions.question: Why can a random train-test split overstate financial model performance?
options: It can mix later regimes, related entities, and overlapping label windows into training and test sets
Random splits always contain too few observations
They prevent a model from learning nonlinear relationships
They automatically include transaction costs
questions.explanation: Financial observations are ordered and often dependent. Temporal, entity, and label overlap can let the evaluation borrow information unavailable in a real deployment.

questions.question: A fraud score ranks transactions well, but the review queue is overloaded. What should change first?
options: Revisit the operating threshold and policy using review capacity and error costs
Declare the model invalid because ranking quality is never useful
Hide low-confidence scores from monitoring
Increase every score by the same constant
questions.explanation: A score becomes an action through policy. Thresholds must reflect false-decline cost, loss tolerance, and available review capacity.

questions.question: Which control should remain independent of a learned trading signal?
options: Pre-set exposure, capital, eligibility, and erroneous-order limits
The model's feature importance ranking
The training loss curve
The candidate's expected return
questions.explanation: Deterministic risk limits prevent a learned signal or software failure from granting itself unbounded market authority.

questions.question: What does independent model validation add to a release decision?
options: Objective challenge of assumptions, implementation, limitations, and outcome evidence
A guarantee that the model will never drift
Permission to skip monitoring after launch
A replacement for accountable business and risk owners
questions.explanation: Independent challenge reduces confirmation bias and tests whether the evidence actually supports the stated use; it does not remove owner accountability.

questions.question: Which monitoring view best detects harm after a financial ML release?
options: Data, score, policy action, override, delayed outcome, and loss metrics by relevant cohort and time
Average API latency without decision outcomes
Training accuracy from the original development set
Total prediction count without policy or customer context
questions.explanation: Operational health must connect changing inputs and scores to actual actions, human interventions, delayed outcomes, and financial consequences.
